mappings.name: requestToPay accepted (202, empty body — the id is the caller's)
duplicate reference is reported as already existing

metadata.why: The adapter must read this as Submitted, not as an error: it is what makes a same-reference retry after a crash safe (docs/flows/crash-safety.md).
A 400 carries the same vocabulary as a FAILED status, so it maps through docs/flows/adapter-mtn-momo.md's table -> invalid_payer.

mappings.name: a payer the rail does not know, selected by MSISDN rather than by reference

why: The same 400 as the `…0400` reference mapping above, selected by the payer
instead. A confirm cannot choose its reference -- the handler mints
provider_reference_id with Uuid::new_v4() before committing the charge, and a
seam to fix it from a test would be a code path that exists only outside
production (AGENTS.md's first rule). The MSISDN, though, comes from the
merchant's own request body, so this is the one matcher an end-to-end confirm
can steer.
It exists for confirm_rails.rs's
a_payer_the_rail_does_not_know_is_a_decline_the_merchant_can_read, which is
the only genuine payer-decline-at-submit in that suite: the case next to it
stages a rotated subscription key, which fails at the TOKEN call and is
provider_account_blocked -- an operator's page, not a payer's problem.
priority 5: below the reference-keyed mappings (priority 1), which must keep
winning for the conformance suite whatever payer they carry, and above the
catch-all 202 (priority 10) that answers every other confirm here.
237600000400 is a documentation MSISDN in the same 2376000000xx block the
conformance charges use, with the 0400 suffix naming the 400 it provokes.

mappings.name: 500 that is really our misconfiguration (MTN's biggest wart)

jsonBody.message: The callback url host is not registered for this API user

metadata.why: Three logical errors arrive as HTTP 500 with a code in the body. Retrying them is an outage that looks like a flake, so the adapter answers ProviderError::Config.

mappings.name: 500 with a body that is not JSON at all

metadata.why: A gateway's own error page, which the adapter must classify as Transport rather than failing to parse it into a decline.

mappings.name: 307 whose Location must never be requested

why: REF_REDIRECT. reqwest's default redirect policy follows up to ten hops and strips
only Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization on a cross-host one, so
Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key, X-Target-Environment, X-Reference-Id and X-Callback-Url
would all be replayed at whatever host the Location named -- and a 307 replays the
request BODY too. vpay_provider::http builds every client with
redirect::Policy::none(), so the adapter must see this 307 itself and answer
ProviderError::Malformed.
The Location points at a mapping on THIS SAME stub on purpose. A cross-host target
would make the case pass for the wrong reason (an unroutable host errors out
whatever the policy is); a same-host path is the hop reqwest follows most eagerly,
so a request recorded against it is proof the policy is gone. See the
`the Location is never requested` mapping below and the __admin/requests/count
assertion in redirects_are_refused_and_never_followed.

mappings.name: the Location is never requested (a 202 if it ever is)

why: Answers the rail's ACCEPTED status deliberately: if redirects were ever followed
again, submit would return Ok(Submitted) and the conformance case's expect_err
would fail loudly -- before the request-count assertion even runs. Two independent
failures for one regression.
